section_summary: This section documents United States interdepartmental deliberations, Allied diplomatic exchanges in the Far Eastern Commission, and SCAP operational policies concerning food relief, cereal allocations, and compulsory crop collections in occupied Japan between June 1946 and March 1947. Officials from the State, War, and Agriculture Departments negotiated civilian import quotas while addressing Soviet and British criticisms regarding Japanese consumption levels and alleged preferential treatment over liberated areas. The materials also trace the dispatch of the 1947 American Food Mission to Japan and Korea and detail SCAP's implementation of emergency rice collection measures, including incentive goods, price bonuses, and Eighth Army surveillance to enforce farm delivery quotas.

subfiles.summary: Telegram reporting on Izvestiya's criticism of the Yoshida government and US authorities for favoring landowners over land reform.

subfiles.about: Recommends advising Whitman that State agrees with the War Department that proposed British amendments on rice collection and polishing are too operational for a policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Recommends advising Whitman that A-H agrees with the War Department that proposed British amendments are too operational.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum on British Amendments to Japanese Food Policy

subfiles.about: Transmits British proposals to amend FEC civilian supply document C2-016 regarding rice collection, milling limitations, and food crisis publicity, requesting the War Department's position.

subfiles.summary: Approves two CAD-requested changes to the FEC food policy paper regarding Japan's economic rehabilitation and internal food distribution.

subfiles.about: Records CAD representative Baldwin's objections to clauses in the draft Japanese food policy paper derived from SWNCC directives.

subfiles.about: Expresses grave concern that the US Delegation has awaited instructions for twenty-eight days after General Hilldring had the food policy paper recommitted to Committee No. 2.

subfiles.about: Presents an unshortened draft policy paper detailing US directives on civilian relief, production obligations, and import controls for adoption by the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.about: Notes that the food policy memorandum had not yet arrived, was too long, and should be shortened.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten notes between Hilldring and Gross regarding the delay and excessive length of the food policy paper.

subfiles.about: Provides an exhaustive analysis of Japan's staple food balance sheet, prefectural collection quotas, emergency incentive programs, legal compulsory delivery powers, and Eighth Army surveillance.
subfiles.from: Natural Resources Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive study analyzes Japan's staple food supply and estimated 1.64-million-ton deficit for the 1947 rice year, detailing quota allocations across all forty-six prefectures and the decline in collections after January 1947. It evaluates emergency measures introduced on March 1, 1947, including bonus payments and the link system providing fertilizers, sake, cigarettes, and consumer goods for rice deliveries, alongside legal mechanisms for compulsory crop expropriation. The report concludes with General MacArthur's directive instructing the Eighth Army to maintain strict surveillance over Japanese prefectural officials and black market operations.
subfiles.title: NRS Preliminary Study No. 6: Japanese Food Collection Program with Emphasis on Collection of the 1946 Rice Crop
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
